content:
Apple TV's current lineup is incredibly strong, featuring hits like "Slow Horses" (formerly "Slow Horses"), "Ted Lasso" ("It's All Good Coach"), "Dark Matter" ("Dark Matter"), and Matthew McConaughey's new comedy "Brothers." But there's even more exciting content coming. Here's everything premiering on Apple TV in October.

The Last First: Winter K2 ("The Last First: Winter K2")

  • Date: October 2
  • Format: Movie
  • Genre: Documentary

"The Last First: Winter K2," directed by Amir Bar-Lev, tells a complex, thrilling, and moving story that takes a deep dive into the extreme mountaineering industry and its ever-evolving culture. The story focuses on a 2021 expedition featuring Icelandic climber John Snorri Sigurjónsson and the Pakistani father-son duo Ali and Sajid Sadpara, whose goal is to become the first people to summit K2 in winter — when the conditions on K2 are at their most brutal. On this perilous climb, they encounter influencer climbers and their camera crews, clients of commercial expedition teams, and renowned Nepali climber Nims and his team of Sherpas. "The Last First: Winter K2" takes viewers to K2's frozen peaks and unpredictable weather, revealing an unexpected, layered story — involving strategy and determination, class and hierarchy, wealth and power — all unfolding in life-or-death conditions.

The Sisters Grimm ("The Sisters Grimm") (Season 2)

  • Date: October 2
  • Format: TV Series
  • Genre: Kids & Family

Two orphaned sisters navigate a town filled with fairy tale characters, interacting with heroes and villains while investigating the mystery of their parents' disappearance. "The Sisters Grimm" blends exploration, fantasy, and adventure, offering important life lessons for viewers of all ages.

Small Prophets ("Small Prophets")

  • Date: October 7
  • Format: TV Series
  • Genre: Comedy

"Small Prophets" is a comedy about eccentric Michael Sleep (Pearce Quigley). Since his beloved Clea disappeared seven years ago, he's been living an extremely mundane life. He works at a hardware store, visits his father Brian (Sir Michael Palin), and hopes for Clea's return. One day, Brian shares an ancient formula using rainwater, horse manure, and a touch of alchemy. Skeptical but willing, Michael decides to follow the formula to create a "homunculus" — a magical sprite that can predict the future — hoping it can answer his most pressing question: "Will I ever see Clea again?"

Matchbox The Movie ("Matchbox The Movie")

  • Date: October 9
  • Format: Movie
  • Genre: Action

"Matchbox The Movie," based on the classic Mattel toy brand, is an action-packed, globe-trotting adventure about a group of lifelong friends whose lives are turned upside down when CIA undercover agent Sean (John Cena) — their long-missing former leader — suddenly returns to their small town. Unknowingly dragged into a wild international chase, they must take on the responsibility of saving the world.

Tenzing ("Tenzing")

  • Date: October 16
  • Format: Movie
  • Genre: Drama

"Tenzing" is based on a true story, recounting the little-known tale of Tenzing Norgay (Genden Phuntsok). A talented Himalayan climber, he joined New Zealand mountaineer Edmund Hillary (Tom Hiddleston) as one of the first people to successfully summit Mount Everest. Encouraged by his wife Dawa (Thinley Lhamo) and supported by expedition secretary Jill Henderson (Caitríona Balfe), they successfully persuaded Colonel John Hunt (Willem Dafoe) to allow Tenzing to join the British expedition as a full member rather than just a porter. Western climbers saw "Everest" as a goal to conquer, but Tenzing revered "Chomolungma" as a sacred goddess of the snow mountains. The subsequent climb had to contend with the tensions of background, class, and ambition, as well as the mountain's many perils. But at the top of the world, empires, status, and desires fade away, leaving only two outsiders bound by mutual respect and trust — for Tenzing, a moment of fulfilling a lifelong dream and spiritual calling.

Where's Wanda? ("Where's Wanda?") (Season 2)

  • Date: October 21
  • Format: TV Series
  • Genre: Dark Comedy

Apple's first German-language series, "Where's Wanda?," is a dark comedy about Dedo and Carlotta Klatt, a couple desperate to find their missing 17-year-old daughter Wanda — who vanished without a trace months ago. When the police fail to crack the case, the family decides to take matters into their own hands, acquiring surveillance equipment with the help of their tech-savvy son Ole. Posing as utility company workers, they install listening devices throughout the neighborhood and half the community, only to discover that behind everyone's front doors, nobody is quite who they seem.

Nocturne ("Nocturne")

  • Date: October 30
  • Format: TV Series
  • Genre: Crime Drama

The story follows Jonah Lynn (Liev Schreiber) — a veteran turned homicide investigator — who is burned out from the high-pressure streets of Philadelphia and moves to a small town in western Pennsylvania hoping for a quiet life. However, when the town and his family fall prey to a cunning serial killer, Jurek Walter (Graham), Jonah must do everything in his power to protect everything he holds dear. While desperately searching for Jurek's last missing victim, Jonah is forced to send his goddaughter, FBI agent Saga Bauer (Beetz), to confront Jurek head-on. How far will Jonah go?

New Episodes: "Slow Horses," "Brothers," and More

Apple TV has multiple currently airing series dropping new episodes throughout October, including:

  • "Slow Horses": The acclaimed British spy thriller airs through October 21
  • "Last Seen" ("Last Seen"): The crime thriller airs through October 7
  • "Slow Horses": The acclaimed British spy thriller airs through October 21
  • "Dark Matter": The sci-fi series starring Joel Edgerton airs through October 30
  • "Brothers": The comedy starring Matthew McConaughey and Woody Harrelson airs through November 4

Which of Apple TV's October releases are you planning to watch? Let us know in the comments.

Apple TV costs $14.99 per month, and you can also subscribe via the Apple One bundle for a discounted rate.
